<text:style bold="true">Geometric Tools</text:style>

<image:base64 col="0" width="34" wrap="none"></image:base64>

The Geometric Tools panel holds the tools that draw the basic figures. Pick a tool,
then click or drag on the drawing area. When a figure is finished it is selected, so
its properties (colours, thickness, ...) can be changed at once in the Properties
panel. Points that start or end on another object snap to it: a constraint keeps
them together. Besides the corners, the middle of each straight side (lines, poly-lines,
polygons, regular shapes, rectangles) and the point where two straight sides cross are
snap points too; the point is then kept at the middle or at the crossing by a constraint. The arrow keys of the keyboard move the selected objects by one unit
at a time (ten with Shift held); Ctrl+Z undoes each press, while a key kept held down is undone as a single step. All the buttons of this
panel are always active.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Select / move</text:style>
The arrow is the normal tool. Click an object to select it (Shift+click adds
more objects), drag it to move it, drag its handles to resize it or to move
       its points. Dragging on empty space selects what the rubber band covers. A
       click with the right button on an object offers the operations that make
       sense for it.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Line</text:style>
Drag from the first point to the second. Holding Shift keeps the line
horizontal or vertical.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Poly-line</text:style>
Click the points one after the other; a double-click or the Enter key ends
the line. It is an open line made of straight sides.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Polygon</text:style>
Like the poly-line, but closed: the last point is joined to the first one and
the figure can be filled. A double-click, Enter or a click on the first point
       ends it.

<image:base64 col="0" width="5" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Rectangle</text:style>
Drag from one corner to the opposite one; Shift makes a square. The small
arrow at its right chooses the kind: rectangle or rectangle with rounded
       corners (the radius is in the properties). The four corners and the four
       sides can take constraints.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Ellipse / circle</text:style>
Drag from the centre: the distance sets the size. It draws an ellipse; keep
Shift pressed (also while dragging) to get a circle. The property "Circle
       (equal radii)" of an ellipse tells if it is a circle: when it is checked the
       vertical radius follows the horizontal one, also when the handles are dragged
       later.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Arc</text:style>
The elliptical arc: drag the ellipse, then click where the arc starts and
where it ends. The small arrow at its right chooses two other ways: arc by
         3 points (the two ends, then a point of the arc) and arc by centre (the
         centre, the start and the end, counter-clockwise).

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Spline</text:style>
A smooth curve through the points that you click; a double-click or Enter
ends it. The points can be moved afterwards.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Text</text:style>
Click where the text goes and type it. Font, size and colour are in the
properties; with the right button the text can be turned into shapes.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Vectorize</text:style>
Recognises simple geometries contained in a raster picture and makes them
vector. Click a uniform area of the picture: if it is a rectangle, an ellipse
       or a straight line, the vector figure is put over it, ready to be edited,
       filled or constrained like any other.

<image:base64 col="0" width="6" wrap="left"></image:base64><text:style bold="true">Regular shape</text:style>
Drag from the centre towards a corner to draw a regular polygon. The number
of sides is in the properties and can be changed later. The shape always
       stays regular, even when a corner is dragged or a constraint is applied. In the
       points mode, dragging a corner resizes and turns the shape about the opposite
       corner (or the middle of the opposite side), which stays where it is, unless
       the constraints force it to move. With the resize handles (first click) a
       regular polygon is scaled evenly (it cannot be stretched), and the corner
       opposite to the handle stays where it is; with
       the right button it can be converted into a polygon or a path, which can then
       be deformed freely.
